User-defined branch-wise kernels

Source: R/kernels_extended.R
k_edge.Rd

Defines a new tree kernel by the variance each edge accumulates, written as a Stan expression. Any kernel of this form is a valid covariance on every tree as long as the edge variances are non-negative, and it keeps the O(N) pruning likelihood and leave-one-out densities.

Usage

k_edge(w, pars = list(), defaults = NULL, name = "edge")

Arguments

w

Stan expression for the edge variances (before scaling by sigma^2).

pars

Named list of parameter bounds, each c(lower, upper). Parameters get uniform priors on these bounds.

defaults

Named list of parameter values used by kernel_plot() and kernel_check(); defaults to the midpoints of the bounds.

name

Short name used in printed output and Stan variable names.

Value

A kernel component.

Details

The expression must return a vector with one element per edge and may use the edge vectors len (length), hs and he (heights of the start and end of the edge above the root), is_tip (1 for tip edges), the tree height Tmax, and the parameters named in pars. Use Stan's elementwise operators .* and ./ between vectors. The same expression is evaluated in R (after translating .*, ./, pow() and square()) for kernel_matrix(), kernel_check() and kernel_plot().

Examples

# Pagel's kappa with a rate trend through time
k <- k_edge("pow(len, kappa) .* exp(beta * he)",
            pars = list(kappa = c(0, 1), beta = c(-5, 5)))
k
#> phylogp kernel: edge("pow(len, kappa) .* exp(beta * he)") 
#>   edge1      edge("pow(len, kappa) .* exp(beta * he)") parameters: sigma, kappa, beta
